title: Singleton tables are not actually constrained to one row

evidence.quote: This is a singleton table - only one row exists
This table should only have one row

reasoning: Both models document singleton semantics, but each row gets a fresh UUID primary key and there is no fixed key or unique singleton column. Concurrent first-access paths can insert multiple rows, after which code that reads the first row can observe or update an arbitrary configuration/settings record, causing divergent schedule/configuration or auto-disable state.
reproduction: Start with an empty database and issue two concurrent requests that create the default ClientConfig or ClientSettings row; both inserts can succeed because the schema has no singleton constraint.
recommendation: Use a deterministic singleton primary key or a unique constant column, update get-or-create code to fetch by that key, and add a migration/cleanup path for any existing duplicate rows.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the repository tests inspected exercise normal single-request creation rather than concurrent first-access or duplicate-row recovery.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create two sessions against an empty database, attempt concurrent get-or-create for ClientConfig and ClientSettings, and assert only one row exists and all callers receive the same row.
minimumFixScope: ClientConfig and ClientSettings schema plus their get-or-create call sites and an Alembic migration to enforce/normalize singleton rows.
